title: The Board Has Two Front Doors

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I have installed a doorbell on Black's home.
directions: [board: the real starting board. White home A one and Black home J ten carry owner badges as well as colour. A small felt welcome mat lies beside each home corner. Pip is screwing a doorbell onto the far corner.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: On their home. Not near it.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Yes. So they know I arrived. And I find out tomorrow whether I stayed.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Hello. Pip has just described the rule we came for.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Ten rows. Ten columns. A Hi, a Sjor and a Muju in White's corner.
directions: [board: the ten by ten grid, rows numbered down the side, columns lettered along the bottom. White Hi on B one, White Sjor on B two, White Muju on A two. Black's three in the far corner.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: White's home is A one, this corner. Black's home is J ten, the far corner.
directions: [board: A one lights. Then J ten lights. Both corner squares are empty.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Same starting team. Different front doors. Two ways to win.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Last piece gone? The game is done.
directions: [board: one side of the board empties, piece by piece. Every removal has an attacker standing next door first. Nothing moves onto a square it emptied.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The other way is to stand on the other player's home.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: You have to still be standing there when your next turn starts.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Arrive. Survive. High five?

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A home threat means standing on the corner that could end the game.
directions: [card: two cards face up on the table. One reads A one. One reads J ten.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Which corner does White have to reach?

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: One card says A one. The other says J ten.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Put a finger on one, or just look at both.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: J ten. Black's home.
directions: [board: a practice position. Black's Hi has stepped off I ten. Black's Sjor stands on J nine. A White Hi walks I ten to J ten along a clear path. The J ten card lights. The A one card goes grey.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A one is White's own home. Your own home threatens nobody.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Now the part that catches people. Does arriving finish the game right there?

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: It does not. My doorbell only says somebody came.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: It did not step on the mat. It reached across.
directions: [board: the turn marker flips to Black. Same position. Black's Sjor stays on J nine and does not move. One bonk reaches across to J ten. The White visitor is removed. The mat lies there with nothing on it.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Pip is right. The visitor has to be there when White's next turn starts.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: And the game has to still be going.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Home waits a turn. The last piece does not.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: The doorbell rang. Then it had nothing to announce.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: We know which door. Nobody has counted the walk.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Now one thing is different. A Black piece is standing on our corner.
directions: [card: EVIDENCE. Proves: J ten is the corner White must reach. Not checked: the path, the reply, the money.]
[board: one thing changes. A Black Hi is standing on A one, on Pip's mat.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Same rule, other direction. Black's next turn start is the moment that matters.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Waiting.
directions: [board: Pip raises a hand and holds it up. One full beat of silence.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Arrive. Survive. Next turn: high five.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: That is enough for today if you want.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: White moves first. Each side starts with a Hi, a Sjor and a Muju. White begins on B one, B two and A two. Black begins on I ten, I nine and J nine.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Next time: how far can one piece walk in one go?

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I am keeping the mats. They say welcome. They do not say for how long.

question: Which corner does White have to reach?
